problem.standards: The DfE's statutory guidance asks designated teachers to make sure school staff have high expectations of children in care and previously in care. One person can't do that alone.
problem.evidence: Delivered at Darlington as a one-day course for all school staff, within the Designated Leaders Programme.

outcomes: Describe what a child in care or with a social worker may bring into school.
Recognise low expectations in everyday phrases, tasks, groupings and displays.
Use the Pygmalion research to explain how expectations reach a child.
Use Maslow and Baumeister and Leary to explain why belonging comes before stretch.
Use a walk-through checklist and Language that Cares to change what holds children back.
Map one child's strengths and write your own named action in the school plan.

pillars.title: Five steps to higher expectations
pillars.stance: Expect more. Then help it happen.
pillars.stance_line: The five sessions of the day, each built on its own research.
items: A child still working out if they are safe has less left for learning. (Maslow)
Adults' beliefs reach a child through grouping, feedback and tone. (Pygmalion)
Displays, seating and jobs tell a child whether they belong. (Baumeister and Leary)
Build stretch on what a child does well. (Dweck)
A named action for every adult
Every member of staff writes one action, with a date it will be reviewed.
pillars.base: The day is designed so your designated teacher can co-lead it, especially the final session on the school plan.

story_line: Two stories run through the day: Priya, 9, at her third school in two years, and Marcus, 15, who wants to be a vet. Each is a composite, drawn from real experiences of care.

facilitator.name: Luke Rodgers BEM
facilitator.line: From care leaver to care leader
paras: Luke went into care at 10. He has spent his career inside children's services as a consultant, trainer and keynote speaker, and is CEO of The Care Leaders.

He has worked with councils nationally on the education of children in care, including Darlington, where designated teachers designed their own programme with him and this day ran for all school staff, and Middlesbrough's town-wide programme to make every school attachment aware and trauma informed.
Teachers are one of the largest groups he trains, and he has spoken at national and regional virtual school conferences.
He was a Knowledge Equity Fellow at Saïd Business School, University of Oxford, and was awarded the British Empire Medal in 2018 for commitment to children and families.
